problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}(3-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}s,$ where $C$ is the ellipse $12{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}=36,$ traversed once in the counterclockwise direction?
worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

Note that we can write the equation of our ellipse in the form

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{(2\sqrt{3})^{2}}=1.
$$

So, the curve $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $\sqrt{3}$ and $2\sqrt{3},$ respectively. Therefore, it can be parametrized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,0\le t<2\pi .
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3{sin}^{2}⁡t+12{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡t+3({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡t+3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=3-{x}^{2},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =3-(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2} \\  & =3-3{cos}^{2}⁡t \\  & =3(1-{cos}^{2}⁡t) \\  & =3{sin}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}(3-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }3{sin}^{2}⁡t\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡t+3}\,\text{d}t \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡t\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡t+3}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
